title: Nicko McBrain - Wikipedia
notes: Michael Henry 'Nicko' McBrain, born 5 June 1952, Hackney, London. First wanted to drum after seeing Joe Morello with the Dave Brubeck Quartet on television; later Ringo Starr, Charlie Watts, Keith Moon, John Bonham and Brian Bennett were his major influences. Pub bands from 14; Streetwalkers (1975), Pat Travers, Trust. Asked to replace Clive Burr in 1982; on every Iron Maiden album from Piece of Mind (1983). Writes all the band's drum parts. 'Where Eagles Dare ... famously displays McBrain's ability to use the single drum pedal very quickly, plus his rapid tom fills' (after the 2004 documentary). Known for not using a double bass pedal; Dickinson: he refused one on Where Eagles Dare, considering them 'undrummerish'; he claims to have used one only on Face in the Sand (Dance of Death); a DW 5000 Accelerator single pedal; barefoot since 2000. 'Octopus', his drum tech says, of the World Slavery Tour. The back end of the left stick for a powerful snare. Rhythms of the Beast: a book of transcriptions (1990) and a video (1991). Paiste cymbals; Sonor drums, then Premier, then British Drum Company (2022); a Sonor Phonic Plus Hi-Tech kit on tour in 1986-87. A stroke in January 2023; retired from touring on 7 December 2024, Simon Dawson taking over live.

title: Nicko McBrain recalls when Adrian Smith wanted double bass drumming on an Iron Maiden song
notes: Metal Wani, 12 September 2019, from Drummerzone's film of An Evening With Nicko McBrain at the UK Drum Show, Manchester, 2018. 'I was quoted years ago saying it's very undrummerish, it's very unmusical.' 'I just felt that I didn't wanna use two, because I found one was hard enough. Why compound the issue with two?' 'I'm not gonna use two. I've been practicing on one forever.' 'I have used a double-bass pedal on a song called Face In The Sand off Dance Of Death': Adrian Smith wanted a particular rhythm, and on one pedal his stamina wasn't there.

title: Iron Maiden's Nicko McBrain says he's 'blessed' to play with Steve Harris
notes: Blabbermouth, 16 December 2019, from Neil Shukla's Cosmo Music interview. 'Now, the gallop with Steve. People say, You got a really fast right foot. To a degree, yes, because I have to complement the rhythm section which is bass and the drummer.' 'When you lock in with your bass player, you've got to find what works for the rhythm part against the bottom end of what he's playing.' 'The Trooper vibe, that's Steve's way of writing.' 'My background is soul, funk and blues'; 'my playing style suited a three-piece band because I wasn't just a straight time keeper.'

title: 'I don't play the Trooper fill anymore': Iron Maiden's Nicko McBrain reveals effects of 2023 mini-stroke
notes: Louder (Metal Hammer), 12 August 2024, from The Washington Tattoo podcast: since the stroke he no longer plays the Trooper fill.

title: Iron Maiden's Nicko McBrain 'can't play certain drum parts' following mini-stroke
notes: Planet Rock, 12 August 2024. 'I don't play the Trooper fill anymore because I can't get it... It's the speed of it.' 'I can't do a 16-note roll going into 32nd-note rolls anymore.' Of Caught Somewhere in Time's middle section, 'all snare drum on the record': 'I can't play it.'

title: Nicko McBrain - Drum Clinic, Hollywood, Florida, 27 January 1988
notes: Mark Adams's film of the clinic (Paiste and Sonor banners), watched as contact sheets at 15:00-18:00 and 50:00-53:00: shoulder-length straight blond hair with a fringe, clean-shaven, a fitted periwinkle-blue long-sleeved top with Paiste and his name down the sleeve, pale lavender-grey trousers, white trainers; at the kit from about 52:30, a silver-grey Sonor with chrome hardware and Paiste cymbals.

title: Iron Maiden - Wikipedia
notes: Formed in Leyton, East London, in 1975 by Steve Harris; a leading band of the new wave of British heavy metal. McBrain from December 1982.

title: Piece of Mind - Wikipedia
notes: Released 16 May 1983. The first album with McBrain, who replaced Clive Burr in December 1982. Written in Jersey (Le Chalet hotel), recorded at Compass Point, Nassau, with Martin Birch. Where Eagles Dare, Flight of Icarus, The Trooper.

title: Powerslave - Wikipedia
notes: Released 3 September 1984; the first album with the same line-up as the one before. Written in Jersey, recorded at Compass Point with Martin Birch, mixed at Electric Lady. Aces High, 2 Minutes to Midnight. The World Slavery Tour, 331 days.

title: Somewhere in Time (Iron Maiden album) - Wikipedia
notes: Released 29 September 1986; the first with guitar synthesisers. Compass Point and Wisseloord, with Martin Birch. Wasted Years, by Adrian Smith alone.

title: Seventh Son of a Seventh Son - Wikipedia
notes: Released 11 April 1988, number one in the UK. Musicland, Munich, with Martin Birch. Can I Play with Madness (number 3), The Evil That Men Do. The last with Adrian Smith until 2000.

title: Fear of the Dark (Iron Maiden album) - Wikipedia
notes: Released 11 May 1992. Recorded at Barnyard Studios, Steve Harris's barn converted for it; the first produced by Harris, the last with Martin Birch. Be Quick or Be Dead, Fear of the Dark.

title: Brave New World (Iron Maiden album) - Wikipedia
notes: Released 29 May 2000; Dickinson and Smith back. Recorded at Guillaume Tell, Paris, with Kevin Shirley, the first album the band recorded live in the studio. The Wicker Man.

title: The Trooper - Wikipedia
notes: Second single from Piece of Mind, 20 June 1983, written by Steve Harris after the Charge of the Light Brigade. AllMusic: 'an all-time genre classic' with 'that trademark galloping rhythm'.

title: Aces High (song) - Wikipedia
notes: Powerslave's opening track and second single, written by Steve Harris; McBrain on drums.

title: 2 Minutes to Midnight - Wikipedia
notes: Powerslave's first single, 6 August 1984, by Smith and Dickinson. Its B-side Mission from 'Arry is a taped backstage argument between Harris and McBrain over an extended drum solo.

title: Wasted Years - Wikipedia
notes: The first single from Somewhere in Time, 1986, written by Adrian Smith alone.

title: Be Quick or Be Dead - Wikipedia
notes: The first single from Fear of the Dark, 13 April 1992, by Dickinson and Gers; 'faster and heavier than most Iron Maiden songs'.

title: The Wicker Man (song) - Wikipedia
notes: The first single from Brave New World, 8 May 2000, by Smith, Harris and Dickinson; co-produced by Kevin Shirley and Harris.
